identity.name: Digilogic Systems Ltd
identity.industry: Defence/aerospace test & measurement (ATE / checkout / RADAR test & simulation)

summary.oneLiner: Niche, asset-light defence-electronics play supplying ATEs, checkout systems and measurement/simulation equipment almost entirely to government end-customers (100% B2G ultimately). Edge is the DcPP "nomination" model: once a prototype/tester is validated for a DRDO/PSU program, Digilogic is written into the production manual as the named supplier for that part-number, converting prototyping wins into low-competition, multi-year production annuities. Growth optionality stacked in FY28-31 from (a) Project UDAN manufacturing scale-up and (b) RF subsystem subsidiary Abhedhya moving up the value chain from "tester of systems" to "maker of subsystems."

Edge is the DcPP "nomination" model: once a prototype/tester is validated for a DRDO/PSU program, Digilogic is written into the production manual as the named supplier for that part-number, converting prototyping wins into low-competition, multi-year production annuities. scorecard (fy26 vs fy25): Listed Jan-2026 on BSE-SME, raised ~₹81 cr.
guidance: FY27 revenue growth guided 20–25% (also stated 25–30%) — same band guided (and missed) for FY26.
Roadmap: target ₹100+ cr of POs in hand by end-Sep-2026 (H1) to underwrite FY27; H1 call to give clarity.
Current setup can support up to ~₹150–160 cr revenue before needing UDAN.
Project UDAN incremental revenue: ₹11–13 cr (FY29), ₹28–30 cr (FY30), ₹57–61 cr (FY31).
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary): no revenue in FY27; first revenue expected FY28.
order book / pipeline: Order book ₹31 cr (₹30+ cr by 30-May-2026), executable/billed largely by Aug-2026.
₹22 cr+ FY26 spillover carried into first week of April (hardware import delays).
Pipeline ~₹110 cr (down from ~₹200 cr); shortfall deferred 6–8 months on GoI fund re-prioritization, "not lost."
Marquee FY26 wins: 4 checkout systems delivered to PSUs; order for 250 units of deployable spectrum monitoring & analysis systems from a defence PSU.
Part of ~5–6 main DcPP programs; 4 critical DcPP programs already in production/deployment.
segment: Revenue mix FY26: measurement equipment ~49%, checkouts ~22%, ATEs ~17% (vs ATE+checkout ~44% in FY25 — shift toward higher-margin, software-heavy measurement gear drove margin gain).
Prototyping ~30% / production ~70% of revenue (prototyping = DRDO; production = defence PSUs like BEL, BDL).
Per missile program, Digilogic's ATE/checkout scope = ~4–6% of total program budget (e.g. ₹15–24 cr on a ₹300–400 cr program), nomination-based once validated (MSQA-validated).
growth drivers: DcPP nomination annuities: production orders travel with squadron deliveries to Air Force/Navy/Army.
Defence-export pull: Indian missile exports (Philippines, Malaysia, Cambodia) carry Digilogic systems (billed via BDL etc.).
Abhedhya RF vertical (radar/EW/comms subsystems — antennas, up/down converters, exciters) — backward integration to cut reliance on partners.
In-house SBC (single-board computer) R&D, positioned vs Curtiss-Wright / Abaco, mil-grade −20 to +85°C.
Aerospace MOUs signed with OEMs Sperry and Eirad to reach Tier-1s (Airbus, Boeing); evaluation phase.
2–3 additional new R&D products in pipeline.
margins: EBITDA margin 19.6% (+152 bps), PAT margin 13.3% (+250 bps), driven by software value-add in measurement equipment (low material cost) and product-mix shift.
Production orders historically deliver "good profitability"; UDAN supplies pre-secured.
capex: Project UDAN: greenfield manufacturing + environmental testing + ATE/checkout production facility, ~4x current capacity (6 systems/6 months → 20–25 systems/6 months), live by mid-2028, targeted at DcPP production.
Guest house under construction (~₹2.1 cr total exposure, not fully drawn); finance cost capitalized; cost of capital REPO + 2.5%.
capital allocation: IPO proceeds (~₹81 cr, Jan-2026) toward growth (UDAN, R&D, RF subsidiary).
Debt nearly eliminated (D/E 0.04x). Heavy reinvestment into R&D and new verticals; no dividend signal.
risks: Import-supply concentration: most integration hardware imported from US/EU OEMs; geopolitics (Iran, Ukraine) doubled lead times (8 wks → ~4 months) → FY26 ₹22 cr+ spillover and missed guidance. Mitigation claimed via OEM re-routing (1–2% costlier).
Guidance credibility: missed FY26 guidance, re-issuing same 20–25% band.
Lumpy, government-budget-dependent order flow; pipeline subject to GoI fund re-prioritization.
Execution/ramp risk on UDAN and unproven Abhedhya RF vertical (revenue only FY28+).
Small-base growth lag vs peers (Data Patterns, Zen Technologies).
mgmt tone: Confident, founder-led, mission-driven; candid on the guidance miss (attributed to import delays, not demand) and on small-base growth criticism. Repeatedly stresses defence growth is "organic," multi-year, cannot be rushed. Personal commitment language from CMD. Maiden call — emphasis on consistent disclosure.
non-obvious: Competitive moat is structural, not technical: once "part-number" nominated in a DcPP production manual, supply is captive — competition only exists at prototyping stage (vs Data Patterns, Zen Technologies).
OEMs reportedly route ~40% of Asia hardware sales to India — gives Digilogic leverage to get OEMs to fix supply routing.
Abhedhya kept as a separate company deliberately — different talent, infra, pay scales than TMS; RF specialists "cannot sit with" tester/simulator engineers.
SBC R&D (~1.5–2 yrs old, 8-member team) stays inside Digilogic (not Abhedhya) — baseband control to pair with Abhedhya's RF for full-system ownership.
~₹150–160 cr is the implicit revenue ceiling of current facilities — UDAN is the real growth unlock.
qoq change log: Maiden investor call (listed Jan-2026 on BSE-SME); no prior concall — this is the FY26 full-year baseline.
FY26 vs FY25: revenue +8.4%, EBITDA +16.5%, PAT +33.8%; margins expanded ~150–250 bps; D/E cut 0.4x→0.04x post-IPO.
Order book fell ₹46 cr → ₹31 cr; pipeline ₹200 cr → ₹110 cr (deferred, not cancelled).
New disclosures vs IPO doc: subsidiary Abhedhya (RF) formed; Project UDAN timeline (mid-2028); UDAN revenue path FY29–31; SBC R&D; Sperry/Eirad aerospace MOUs; 250-unit spectrum-monitoring order.
FY26 guidance (20–25%) missed (actual +8.4%) — attributed to import lead-time blowout; same band re-guided for FY27 with Sep-2026 ₹100+ cr PO milestone as proof-point.

themes.title: Defence indigenization & order-book visibility
themes.need: Indigenization mandates (IDDM / Atmanirbhar / DcPP) plus multi-year order books make domestic defence the cleanest revenue-conversion theme - across electronics, drones, simulators, explosives/munitions and precision systems. BEL guides >INR55k cr FY27 inflow (~INR30k cr QRSAM pending CCS clearance, guided by September) on a INR72,258cr order book; HAL book ~INR2.55 lakh cr; SOLARINDS defence revenue +94% to INR2,634cr FY26, guided >INR4,500cr FY27 on an ~INR18,000cr defence order book (Bhargavastra counter-drone trials completing CY2026); DATAPATTNS inflows strong; BHARATFORG/BEML add land-systems and platforms.
themes.driver: Backlog-to-revenue conversion underway; BEL's QRSAM CCS clearance (guided by Sep-2026, ~INR30k cr of the FY27 inflow guide) is the load-bearing near-term catalyst; fresh MoD orders + emergency procurement; HAL LCA Mk-1A ramp (gated on GE engines).

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.
